title: Gaussian Differential Assessment of Sequential STEM Radiation Damage in Beam-Sensitive Materials
content: Electron radiation damage presents significant challenges in the characterization of sensitive materials using transmission electron microscopy (TEM), particularly in atomic-resolution high-angle annular dark-field scanning transmission electron microscopy (HAADF-STEM) imaging [1]. Despite the use of low-dose approaches, high-energy electron beams can inevitably induce structural defects and chemical modifications, significantly altering the intrinsic structure-property relationships of beam-sensitive materials such as garnet-type Li7La3Zr2O12 (LLZO), a promising lithium-ion conductor as a chemically and thermally stable solid electrolyte for next-generation all-solid-state batteries [2]. Leveraging advanced in situ TEM techniques to enable real-time observation of sensitive energy materials also requires effective control of beam-induced damage, typically by reducing atomic mobility at lower temperatures through cryo-TEM [3]. This further necessitates the quantitative assessment of beam-induced degradation, as qualitative methods often omit subtle yet significant structural changes. To address this, we have developed a method using a pre-trained convolutional neural network (CNN) to conduct feature-based assessments of electron beam damage, while this method faces limitations related to the reduced spatial resolution due to image patching, domain differences, high-noise environments, and atomic drifts that may introduce pixel misalignment and affect reliability [4].
